Netanyahu Moves to Fully Lock Down West Bank Ahead of Israeli Elections
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered preparations for a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank and the complete closure of the city of Hebron. Earlier today, Israeli forces killed two Palestinians who had reportedly shot five Israeli soldiers near an illegal settlement. Two of the Israeli soldiers died. After the attack, Israel’s far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called for Israel to restrict the movement of Palestinians across the occupied West Bank.
Itamar Ben-Gvir: “Their movements on the road should be stopped. We must stop allowing them from driving on the roads of Judea and Samaria. The lives of our residents of Judea and Samaria, of our citizens, our soldiers, our police officers and our fighters, are a million times more important than the freedom of movement.”
This comes amid escalating attacks by Israeli settlers and soldiers in the run-up to Tuesday’s elections in Israel. Israeli troops conducted raids across the West Bank today, detaining dozens of Palestinians. Meanwhile, Israeli authorities detained 11 foreign activists Thursday after participating in a Palestinian olive harvest in the West Bank. On Wednesday, Israeli forces briefly detained 80 rabbis, volunteers and activists accompanying Palestinian farmers. Those detained included New York congressional candidate Brad Lander.
Topics:
Israel & Palestine
As Trump Threatens New Strikes, U.S. Ambassador Says Iran War Could Last Another Year
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz has told the Financial Times that the U.S. war on Iran could last another year. This comes as President Trump has threatened to launch new strikes on Iran, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that overthrowing Iran’s government remains Israel’s “primary objective.” A senior Iranian official told Drop Site News that Tehran’s latest intelligence assessment indicates a high likelihood that the U.S. and Israel could launch a large-scale bombing campaign before Tuesday’s Israeli elections.
Topics:
Iran
Study: European Heat Waves Killed 50,000 in 2026 as Toll of Climate Crisis Grows
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
In climate news, a new study finds this year’s summer heat waves in Europe killed a staggering 50,000 people, with climate change responsible for two-thirds of the deaths. The study looked at deaths in 854 cities, but not deaths that occurred in rural areas, meaning the actual death toll is likely far higher.
Topics:
Climate Crisis
French Student Union Denounces Macron Ban on “Illegitimate” Protests
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
French President Emmanuel Macron has banned what he called “illegitimate” demonstrations across France following weeks of student-led protests. Macron said the ban extends to all demonstrations not organized by unions. France’s main student union blasted Macron’s order, saying, “Macron is trampling upon the freedom to protest in our country, and is spitting on the values of ​the republic he claims to defend.”
On Thursday, students rallied in Paris after being given last-minute approval to protest.
Lao: “It’s important, because if we give in to pressure, if we give in to fear, unfortunately, we won’t achieve anything. That’s why today we need to mobilize. We must not give up, because, for the moment, we’re not being listened to, and we will carry on until we’re heard.”
Topics:
France
Serbia: 150,000 Rally in Student-Led Protest Ahead of Sunday’s Election
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
In Serbia, about 150,000 protesters demonstrated in Belgrade in a student-led rally against longtime Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić. On Sunday, Serbia will hold parliamentary elections that could decide whether Vučić’s ruling party keeps control. The student movement is running 250 candidates in the election. At Thursday’s rally, protesters decried the Serbian government.
Bogdan Pavković: “It means changing of this awful, horrendous system, which cheats on us, which spies on us, which beats us. We want to support healthy bases like love, compassion. We want to have a normal economy, normal education to support all the values which will grow us together in the future.”
Topics:
Serbia
Students Lead Protests in Indonesia over Economic Crisis & Forest Fires
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
In Indonesia, student-led protests over unemployment, rising fuel costs and forest fires are continuing. On Thursday, hundreds of students rallied in Banjarmasin, which has been blanketed by haze from fires.
Rizky: “What we’re seeing today is a reflection of the fact that our anger has reached its peak.”
Topics:
Indonesia
Press Crackdown in Egypt: Mada Masr Editor Lina Attalah Referred to Trial
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
The Egyptian government is escalating its crackdown on press freedom. On Thursday, the prominent independent journalist Lina Attalah was referred to trial on charges of operating a website without a license. Attalah is the editor-in-chief of the news site Mada Masr. She was questioned by prosecutors for six hours earlier this week. This comes just weeks after Egyptian authorities arrested six journalists at the investigative media platform Matsadaash, detaining the entire newsroom.
Topics:
Egypt
Elon Musk Invests $1 Billion in Skydance, Threatens Democratic Lawmakers
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
Elon Musk has invested about $1 billion in Skydance, the massive entertainment and media conglomerate. Earlier this month, Paramount Skydance completed its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, bringing CBS, CNN, HBO, Paramount+ and other major media properties under the same ownership. Skydance CEO David Ellison and his father Larry are major supporters of President Trump.
This comes at a time when Elon Musk has spent $366 million in the current election cycle to help Republicans. On Wednesday, Musk posted a warning to Democratic lawmakers who are threatening to investigate him if they gain control of Congress after the midterms. Musk wrote on his social media platform X, “Live by the sword, die by the sword. Those who pick fights with me should understand that I will find out who is really pulling the strings and come for them, not just their puppets…”
Book Claims Saudi and Emirati Leaders Set Up Secret Bank Accounts for Jared Kushner
Oct 23, 2026
Image Credit: Daniel Torok
Link copied
Vanity Fair has published an excerpt from a forthcoming book about Jared Kushner alleging that Saudi and Emirati leaders secretly put at least $2 billion into bank accounts for Kushner after he promised to push their agenda with President Trump, his father-in-law. Journalist Matthew Cole reports Dutch spies learned of the secret arrangement after hacking into Kushner’s iPhone. Cole also reports Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu encouraged Kushner to deposit some of the money in the Israeli central bank. Kushner denied the report, saying, “The allegations made by this author are completely insane, categorically false, and never happened.”
NYT: Justice Department Investigates Ex-DHS Adviser Corey Lewandowski
Oct 23, 2026
Image Credit: Grzegorz Wajda / SOPA Images via Reuters Connect
Link copied
The New York Times is reporting the Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into Corey Lewandowski. Sources told the paper the probe is investigating whether he profited from his role as a top adviser to former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.
Ecuador: Opposition Leader Arrested in Noboa’s Widening Crackdown on Left
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
In Ecuador, former leftist presidential candidate Luisa González has been arrested on alleged campaign financing irregularities. González is an ally of former President Rafael Correa. She denied the accusations as “absurd” and said they were politically motivated. Her arrest comes amid intensifying attacks on the opposition by the government of right-wing, Trump-backed Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa. This is the head of the leftist Citizens’ Revolution party.
Gabriela Rivadeneira: “What has just occurred is part of a systematic campaign to try to silence opposition voices in this country. A dictatorship is being established in this country, in Ecuador, promoted by the permanent breakdown of the rule of law, the breakdown of the democratic system.”
Topics:
Ecuador
Cuba Accuses U.S. of Threatening to Punish Nations Who Support U.N. Resolution Against Embargo
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
Cuba has accused the Trump administration of threatening countries with tariffs, travel restrictions and other retaliatory sanctions to pressure them into voting against an upcoming United Nations resolution demanding the U.S. lift its decadeslong economic embargo on Cuba. For decades, a majority of the U.N. General Assembly has opposed the economic blockade. This is Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez.
Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla: “These methods of pressure include the threat of imposing punitive tariffs; the suspension of cooperation programs; the denial of visas to government officials, their family members and their children; support for forces opposed to the respective governments; the threat of encouraging overthrow or subversion; interference in election processes; and the threat of politically destabilizing those countries.”
Topics:
Cuba
ICE Agents Filmed Trying to Rip Toddlers from Guatemalan Father’s Arms in Providence
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
In Providence, Rhode Island, anger is mounting after a video went viral showing ICE agents attempting to arrest a Guatemalan father as he held his two distraught toddlers in his arms. Two agents are seen repeatedly trying to rip the two young children from their father. The man, who has only identified himself as Sebastian, said he was taking his young children to their babysitter before heading to work in construction.
A woman recording the video is heard confronting the agents, asking them for a warrant. One of the agents threatened to pepper-spray her, screaming in her face that she needed to stay at least 25 feet away.
The agents ultimately let the man go, telling him to report to ICE in a few days or they would arrest his entire family. Massachusetts Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley said in a statement, “Where is our humanity? How is this keeping anyone safe?”
Topics:
Immigrant Rights
Pentagon OKs Testing Heat Ray Weapon on Migrants Along U.S.-Mexico Border
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
CNN reports the Pentagon has authorized the Department of Homeland Security to test a nonlethal “heat ray” for potential use on migrants at the U.S.-Mexico border. U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth signed the memo last month, allowing DHS to test the military-grade weapon. The so-called Active Denial System shoots an invisible energy beam that reportedly causes a burning sensation that penetrates the skin. Its electromagnetic waves can reach more than half a mile away. The U.S. military briefly deployed the heat ray weapon to Afghanistan nearly 20 years ago but never used it in combat.
DOJ Charges Virginia Senate Leader, Louise Lucas
Oct 23, 2026
Image Credit: Facebook/L. Louise Lucas
Link copied
The Trump administration has charged one of the most powerful Democratic lawmakers in Virginia with racketeering and money laundering conspiracy in connection to a cannabis business she co-owns with family members. Six other people were indicted, as well.
Virginia state Senator Louise Lucas serves as president pro tempore in the Virginia Senate. She is the first woman and first African American to hold that position. Lucas has also been a vocal critic of President Trump.
In recent years, the Trump administration has targeted numerous high-profile Black women, including Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, New York Attorney General Letitia James, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis in Georgia and New Jersey Congresswoman LaMonica McIver.
Polling Firm Admits It Fabricated Polls
Oct 23, 2026
Link copied
A polling firm cited by major news outlets has admitted it fabricated its data. Wedgewood Polls made the admission after the polling website FiftyPlusOne raised questions about its polls. It remains unclear who was behind Wedgewood. In a statement, the firm said it released fake polls to “demonstrate the vulnerabilities, lack of oversight, and overall low barrier to entry in the modern political polling industry.” The fake polls may have affected real political races. In June, Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Mallory McMorrow dropped out of the race shortly after a fake Wedgewood poll suggested her support was plummeting. McMorrow said the fake poll “killed” her campaign.

Netanyahu ordena un bloqueo total de Cisjordania en vísperas de las elecciones en Israel
23 Oct. 2026
Link copied
El primer ministro de Israel, Benjamín Netanyahu, ha ordenado preparar un bloqueo total en los territorios ocupados de Cisjordania y el cierre completo de la ciudad de Hebrón. En la mañana de este viernes, las fuerzas armadas de Israel mataron a dos palestinos que, según se informa, habían disparado contra cinco soldados israelíes cerca de un asentamiento ilegal, dos de los cuales murieron. Después del ataque, el ministro de Seguridad Nacional israelí, el ultraderechista Itamar Ben-Gvir, abogó para que Israel restrinja la circulación de palestinos en los territorios ocupados de Cisjordania.
Itamar Ben-Gvir: “Hay que impedir que circulen por las carreteras. Debemos dejar de permitirles circular por las carreteras de Judea y Samaria. Las vidas de nuestros residentes de Judea y Samaria, de nuestros ciudadanos, nuestros soldados, nuestros policías y nuestros combatientes, son un millón de veces más importantes que la libertad de circulación”.
Judea y Samaria es un término bíblico para referirse a la actual Cisjordania.
Esto se produce en medio de una escalada de ataques perpetrados por colonos y soldados israelíes, en vísperas de las elecciones que se celebrarán el martes en Israel. Este viernes, las fuerzas armadas israelíes llevaron a cabo incursiones en Cisjordania y detuvieron a decenas de palestinos. Asimismo, las autoridades israelíes detuvieron el jueves a once activistas extranjeros que participaron junto con palestinos en una cosecha de aceitunas. El miércoles, militares israelíes retuvieron por varias horas a 80 rabinos, voluntarios y activistas que colaboraban con agricultores palestinos en la recolección. Entre los detenidos se encontraba Brad Lander, candidato al Congreso de Estados Unidos en representación de un distrito de Nueva York.
Temas:
Israel y Palestina
Trump amenaza con lanzar nuevos ataques contra Irán al tiempo que el embajador de EE.UU. ante la ONU afirma que la guerra podría durar un año más
23 Oct. 2026
Link copied
El embajador de Estados Unidos ante las Naciones Unidas, Mike Waltz, le dijo al periódico Financial Times que la guerra de Estados Unidos contra Irán podría durar un año más. Esto se produce al tiempo que el presidente Trump ha amenazado con lanzar nuevos ataques contra Irán. Por su parte, el primer ministro israelí, Benjamín Netanyahu, afirmó que derrocar al Gobierno de Irán sigue siendo el “objetivo principal” de Israel. En declaraciones al medio Drop Site News, un alto funcionario iraní dijo que una nueva evaluación de inteligencia de Teherán indica que es muy probable que Estados Unidos e Israel lancen una campaña de bombardeos a gran escala antes de las elecciones israelíes del martes.

Irán
Un estudio concluye que las olas de calor en Europa causaron 50.000 muertes en 2026 al tiempo que aumentan las víctimas mortales vinculadas a la crisis climática
23 Oct. 2026
Link copied
En noticias sobre el clima, un nuevo estudio concluye que las olas de calor del verano de 2026 en Europa dejaron un alarmante saldo de 50.000 muertes y que el cambio climático fue responsable de dos tercios de ellas. El estudio analizó las muertes registradas en 854 ciudades, pero no las que ocurrieron en áreas rurales, por lo que es probable que el número real de muertes sea mucho mayor.
Temas:
Crisis climática
El principal sindicato de estudiantes de Francia denuncia la prohibición de Macron de las protestas “ilegítimas”
23 Oct. 2026
Link copied
El presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, ha prohibido en todo el país las manifestaciones que califica de “ilegítimas”, tras varias semanas de protestas lideradas por estudiantes. Macron afirmó que la prohibición se extiende a todas las manifestaciones que no son convocadas por sindicatos. El principal sindicato de estudiantes de Francia criticó duramente la orden de Macron y afirmó al respecto: “Macron está pisoteando el derecho a la protesta en nuestro país y está escupiendo sobre los valores de la república que dice defender”.
El jueves, miles de estudiantes marcharon en París tras recibir una autorización de último momento para la movilización.
Lao: “Es importante, porque si cedemos a la presión, si cedemos al miedo, lamentablemente no conseguiremos nada. Por eso hoy tenemos que movilizarnos. No debemos rendirnos, porque de momento no nos están escuchando y seguiremos hasta que lo hagan”.
Temas:
Francia
Unas 150.000 personas participan en Serbia en una protesta liderada por estudiantes en vísperas de las elecciones del domingo
23 Oct. 2026
Link copied
En Serbia, unas 150.000 personas salieron a las calles de la ciudad de Belgrado en una manifestación liderada por estudiantes contra el líder serbio Aleksandar Vučić, quien ha sido primer ministro o presidente durante los últimos 12 años. Vučić renunció en septiembre a la presidencia para postularse de nuevo al cargo de primer ministro. El domingo, Serbia celebrará elecciones parlamentarias anticipadas, que podrían determinar si el partido gobernante de Vučić mantiene el control. El movimiento estudiantil está postulando 250 candidatos en las elecciones. Durante la movilización del jueves, los manifestantes denunciaron las actuaciones del Gobierno serbio.
Bogdan Pavković: “Significa cambiar este sistema espantoso y horrendo, que nos engaña, nos espía y nos golpea. Queremos promover valores saludables, como el amor y la compasión. Queremos tener una economía normal y una educación normal que sustenten todos los valores que nos permitirán crecer juntos en el futuro”.

President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both defended Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy after his campaign released a TV ad that appears to accuse Democratic nominee Amy Acton of lying about being sexually abused as a child. Acton’s stepfather was indicted in 1978 on charges of sexually assaulting her when she was between 10 and 12 years old, though he fled before he could be convicted. Acton’s mother, who lost custody of her two children, sided with her husband and remained with him as a fugitive until his death in 2004. In the controversial campaign ad, the elderly Donna Arthur says her daughter Amy has “lied her entire life” and can’t be trusted as governor, which has been widely interpreted as casting doubt on what Acton has said about being abused as a minor.
“Vivek Ramaswamy is now using that personal trauma as an effort to exploit what she went through and win this race,” says Abby Vesoulis, a reporter for Mother Jones. “He’s currently polling beneath Amy Acton, which shows, I think, that this ad is a desperate attempt to somehow pull off a victory despite poor odds.”
Vesoulis says outrage over the ad, even among Republican voters, is tied to simmering anger about how the Trump administration has handled the Epstein files. She also discusses abuse allegations against Ohio Republican Congressmember Max Miller, who is running for reelection.

Transcript
This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.
AMY GOODMAN: In the Ohio governor’s race, an attack ad has set off a firestorm of criticism from Democrats and many Republicans. Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, a tech billionaire, says he will spend $4 million more to promote the ad ahead of the midterm elections, even though it’s drawn criticism from members of his own party.
The ad features his Democratic opponent Dr. Amy Acton’s estranged mother, in which she denies her daughter was sexually abused as a child. This is a brief clip.
DONNA ARTHUR: I love my daughter, but when I saw her lying about her opponent, it’s not easy for a mother to say this, but Amy has a serious problem.
AMY GOODMAN: The ad first began circulating on social media earlier this week. Dr. Acton responded to her mother’s appearance in the ad in a statement, saying, quote, “Between the ages of 10 and 12, I was sexually abused by her husband, while my birth mother did nothing to protect me. … My birth mother’s husband was arrested, charged with rape, and indicted by a grand jury. At 12 years old, I testified in court. I haven’t seen my birth mother since that day in 1978. She and her husband fled the state and he was declared a fugitive,” she wrote. Dr. Acton also addressed the ad in a campaign stop Wednesday evening.
DR. AMY ACTON: But I’ve never attacked his family. I would never do that. This is despicable, what he’s done. And, you know, you can see that there are so many people who have experienced trauma and abuse in their lives. I’m running for governor because I won’t look the other way while bad actors, special interests keep taking my state backwards on nearly every single measure.
AMY GOODMAN: Ohio’s Republican Senator Jon Husted, who’s in a tight race against Democratic candidate Sherrod Brown, the former senator, said he would not have run the ad. And Ohio’s current governor, Republican Mike DeWine, condemned the ad, calling it “wrong.” This audio is a bit rough, but listen carefully.
GOV. MIKE DEWINE: It’s wrong to run this ad. And even at this late time, my wife Fran saw the ad run this morning on TV. I would just urge the Ramaswamy campaign to take this down.
AMY GOODMAN: But also on Wednesday, Vice President and former Ohio Senator JD Vance said he’d been left feeling “disgusted” — not by Ramaswamy’s ad, but by Republican pushback against it.
VICE PRESIDENT JD VANCE: I’m a little bit disgusted when I see Republicans across the country who are whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America.

Brazilian voters are heading to the polls on Sunday for the presidential runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and far-right Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, with polls showing a tight race that will decide whether Brazil remains led by the left or joins the right-wing surge across Latin America.
We speak to reporter Laís Martins of The Intercept Brasil.

Transcript
This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.
AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman in Los Angeles, with Juan González in Chicago.
We go now to Brazil, where Sunday’s presidential runoff could determine the future of Latin America’s largest democracy. The incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is facing off against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro. The elder Bolsonaro is currently in house arrest for decades for his role in a failed military coup and assassination plot after he lost to Lula in 2022. Despite his father’s attempted coup, Flávio Bolsonaro is the front-runner in Sunday’s race, after coming out slightly ahead in the first round of voting earlier this month, and he promises to free his father.
Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sparred in their first and only debate Sunday, a week before the presidential runoff. During the debate, Lula attacked Bolsonaro for supporting his father’s response to the COVID pandemic. This is a portion of their debate. This is Flávio Bolsonaro speaking first.
SEN. FLÁVIO BOLSONARO: [translated] The PT, the Workers’ Party, has been governing Brazil for 20 years, and nothing has changed or improved for you when it comes to healthcare.
PRESIDENT LUIZ INÁCIO LULA DA SILVA: [translated] Only someone who knows nothing about healthcare, someone who has never used the public health system, could say something like that. They had a four-year run, and it was the greatest disaster in this country’s history: 716,000 people died due to the government’s irresponsibility. Half of those deaths could have been prevented if they had listened to science, if they had believed in science, but they didn’t.
AMY GOODMAN: Meanwhile, President Lula has requested the disqualification of Flávio Bolsonaro over alleged interference by social media company Meta. The president’s petition, filed to Brazil’s top electoral court Wednesday, accuses Meta of limiting the reach of Lula’s posts on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp to boost Bolsonaro’s campaign. This comes after a report led by U.N. special rapporteur on freedom of expression expressed concern over discrepancies in the ability of each campaign to reach voters over Meta’s platforms. Meta has denied favoritism.
For more, we’re joined now from São Paulo, Brazil, by Laís Martins, a reporter with The Intercept Brasil, where she covers technology, politics and human rights. Her latest piece is headlined “Exclusive: Flávio Bolsonaro Paid 600,000 Reais to a Company in the U.S. That Sells an AI System to Manipulate Elections.”
Welcome to Democracy Now!, Laís. If you can explain what you found in this explosive exposé?
LAÍS MARTINS: Thank you, Amy. Sure.
So, the story that we published just last week was based on reports from a whistleblower in the United States, this citizen that came to us with material, including troves of data and documents, showing that this company, called Elytron Cybersecurity, a company that is based out of Brazil but also out of Portugal, that has been hired by the Flávio Bolsonaro campaign, had reportedly, allegedly, offered manipulation, political manipulation, services to people connected to the Trump campaign in 2024.
It’s important to say there is no confirmation as to whether the Trump campaign effectively hired the service or the Flávio Bolsonaro campaign hired the service. But the motivation for this whistleblower to come to us was that the material and the capabilities of this tool that he saw were so serious that he decided to reach out to reporters in Brazil once he saw that the Flávio Bolsonaro campaign had hired this same company.

At least 59 people have died in ICE custody since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term, the highest number in more than a decade. Many deaths have been linked to medical neglect, including four of five recent deaths at California’s Adelanto Processing Center, according to a 2026 report by the state attorney general. Al Jazeera English’s Fault Lines investigated deaths at the facility, which is operated by the private prison company GEO Group, in the new documentary Dying in Detention.
“GEO Group has made over a billion dollars in profits from immigration detention. They have given more than a million dollars … to help reelect Donald Trump,” says correspondent Natasha Del Toro. “That raises a lot of questions for us about the relationship between GEO and the federal government, and some of these conflicts of interest.”

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman in Los Angeles. Juan González is in Chicago.
We’re turning now to the rising numbers of deaths in ICE custody. At least 59 people have died in immigration detention since the start of Trump’s second term, the highest in more than a decade, and a growing number of people are dying from medical neglect. Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias, a 56-year-old legal permanent resident who died earlier this month at an ICE detention center run by the private GEO Group in Laredo, Texas, has complained to his daughter for months about the lack of medical care in detention. At the Adelanto Processing Center, just north of where I am right now in Los Angeles, four out of five recent deaths were linked to substandard medical care. That’s according to the California attorney general’s report on ICE detention centers in California this year.
Journalist Natasha Del Toro and Al Jazeera’s Fault Lines investigated the deaths at the Adelanto Processing Center, which is run, yes, again, by the private GEO Group. This is a clip from the Fault Lines episode Dying in Detention.

Transcript
This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.
AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman in Los Angeles, with Nermeen Shaikh in New York.
We’re continuing our conversation with the acclaimed writer Arundhati Roy. She spoke in New York earlier this week at the People’s AI Summit, and she has a new essay on AI in Equator magazine. It’s headlined “Apocalypse Now and Then.”
Arundhati, thanks so much for staying with us. Why, in an essay on AI, do you say “Apocalypse Now and Then”?
ARUNDHATI ROY: Well, when I started thinking about writing this piece, I just saw that young whistleblower who came out of Anthropic, Jacob Coxon, you know, warning us that they were building something that sounded like the Manhattan Project on steroids, except that the scientists were all driven by, you know, the idea of profit and “we’ve got to get there first.” And then I was bemused by the fact that all the CEOs came out and discussed it and sort of, more or less, informed us that, you know, our future as a species was in their hands, but they were going to take care.
And then you realize that somehow this had a little to do with, obviously, the fact that AI did contain risks — they say around 10% or something — of eliminating the human race, but it was also something that was being put on the market, our apocalypse. You know, we were — they were going to have an IPO. And, you know, the more lethal they sounded, the more dangerous they sounded, the more irreducible they sounded, you know, it was going to drive up their value. So, initially, it was called “Apocalypse Now: Buy Ours, Get Yours Free.” You know? And then, so, that’s why I call it that.
NERMEEN SHAIKH: But you also ask, right at the beginning of the essay, “Are we being gradually locked out of language?” Explain what you mean by that and why you think that is what may eventually happen.
ARUNDHATI ROY: Well, because, as a writer, I’ve watched what’s happening in the world of literature, in public — in the publishing industry with agents, with students, and AI has just crashed into it like a brick through the windscreen, you know? So, you’re seeing publishers having to look at new writers’ work like detectives inspecting crime scenes. You’ve had scandal after scandal of, you know, prizes being given to works that were then done by AI. Yesterday, I read that there’s a new prize for AI writing.
And you have — and I also said it because you have myself as one of hundreds of thousands of writers whose work was just taken without our permission by Anthropic to train their large language models. And then I get a notice, because of a class-action suit, saying, “Oh, we’ll give you 2,000, you know, dollars per book,” or something. I mean, books that people like myself have spent a lifetime trying to write, a lifetime trying to develop a language that is yours, a lifetime trying to explain your background, your culture, your thoughts, your way of living. I mean, this complete lack of understanding of literature. They’ve done the same, you know, with taking people’s voices, people’s likeness, people’s paintings.
And now what? You press a button and say, “Write a novel like Arundhati Roy,” or “Give me this, you know, in such and such a style.” It’s a kind of — you know, these are supposed to be intelligent people, but you see a kind of absolute, opaque denseness to understanding what human beings are, what human civilization is. It’s like corporatizing and privatizing the history of human endeavor, the history of literature, the history of civilization. I mean, it’s the same thing. I know even mathematicians are feeling the same as writers are. You know, what do you think of? Everything’s just a product to be sold on the market, owned by you? I mean, Sam Altman said intelligence — “We see intelligence as a commodity to be sold by the meter”? You know, whose intelligence? Not yours, certainly. Ours, our collective intelligence, stolen from the human race and corporatized by these handful of white men, you know?

One of the most closely watched races in the midterm elections is in Michigan between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers. El-Sayed is a former public health official who is campaigning on a platform of Medicare for All, ending military aid to Israel, and getting corporate money out of politics. Rogers is a former Republican congressman backed by President Trump.
If elected, El-Sayed would become the first Muslim to serve in the U.S. Senate. During Wednesday’s debate in Michigan, Rogers repeated the claim, without providing evidence, that El-Sayed has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied the accusation.
“If Abdul El-Sayed wins, it will be a reminder that the left can win in a swing state like Michigan,” says Mehdi Hasan, editor-in-chief of Zeteo. “And it will be actually a moment to say, 'You know what? Americans rejected Islamophobia.'”

Transcript
This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.
AMY GOODMAN: We are less than two weeks away from the November 3rd midterm elections that’ll determine control of Congress. To win the Senate, Democrats need to flip four Republican seats and hold three of their own, including Michigan, one of the most closely watched races. Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers are in a tight race for an open seat. El-Sayed is a former public health official who’s campaigning on a platform of Medicare for All, ending military aid to Israel, and getting corporate money out of politics. Rogers is a former Republican congressmember backed by President Trump.
On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, has plans to quietly give up to $9 million to a super PAC supporting Mike Rogers. The money started being given after October 14th, which meant the money will not need to be disclosed until after the election.
On Wednesday, the Senate candidates in Michigan met in their final debate. Dr. El-Sayed criticized Rogers’ connection to AIPAC and his support for the war on Iran.
DR. ABDUL EL-SAYED: He’s still cheerleading the war that you are paying for, a war we never should have fought in the first place. You send this man to the U.S. Senate, do not be surprised when we fight more wars, we accrue more national debt, and he does not stand up for you for the price of your gas or the price of your groceries. Why? He’s bought off by the same weapons manufacturers. AIPAC, we just heard, is going to put, what, $9 million into his campaign in the next two weeks alone? Well, that’s what you get when you have an AIPAC-backed politician.
NERMEEN SHAIKH: The New York Times broke the news about AIPAC’s plans to spend $9 million to help Rogers on the same day that AIPAC announced that it will stop endorsing candidates or making direct contributions through its PAC, but it confirmed it will continue influencing elections through its super PAC, United Democracy Project, and other fundraising tools. During the Democratic primary, AIPAC’s super PAC spent more than $30 million in an unsuccessful effort to defeat El-Sayed. The New York Times reports AIPAC decided to spend heavily to help Mike Rogers, after he welcomed AIPAC’s support when asked this question by the moderator during their first debate.
RICK ALBIN: Congressman Rogers, Axios reported that your allies asked AIPAC not to advertise on your behalf, and Axios also reported that you talked with the chair of AIPAC, and the next day they discontinued an ad on your behalf. Do you welcome AIPAC’s public support, given that you do support many pro-Israeli positions? You have 60 seconds.
MIKE ROGERS: Anybody that wants to help my campaign stop a guy who can’t condemn terrorism in our own country because he’s so close to the people who are supporting the Muslim Brotherhood —
DR. ABDUL EL-SAYED: Again, I’ve condemned them.
MIKE ROGERS: — you bet, I’ll take all of that help.

Saudi Arabia Executes Bangladeshi Man and Woman in Mecca
HeadlineOct 21, 2026
Link copied
Saudi Arabia executed a Bangladeshi man and woman in Mecca last week after convicting them of a supposed “indecent act” inside a mosque. Bangladesh says it was not informed of the execution. The execution has sparked public outcry in Bangladesh, since more than 3 million Bangladeshis work and live in Saudi Arabia. According to Amnesty International, Saudi Arabia has executed around 100 people this year; many of them were foreigners convicted of drug offenses.
